content.text:
The panel and MCP crash on startup because `users_email_confirmed_at_v1` sends psycopg a literal `%` inside a `LIKE` pattern. That migration is not recorded as applied, so every boot retries it and exits 1.

`_ensure_users_email_confirmed_at` backfills existing Google and local users, and skips password accounts (`google_sub` like `password-…`):

```654:663:relocation_jobs/core/migrations.py
def _ensure_users_email_confirmed_at(conn) -> None:
    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email_confirmed_at TEXT")
    conn.execute(
        """
        UPDATE users
        SET email_confirmed_at = COALESCE(email_confirmed_at, created_at)
        WHERE email_confirmed_at IS NULL
          AND (google_sub IS NULL OR google_sub NOT LIKE 'password-%%')
        """
    )
```

`conn.execute` always passes parameters, so psycopg treats `%` as a placeholder. `'password-%'` became `%'`, which is not `%s`, `%b`, or `%t`. The same file already escapes literals as `%%` (see the Workday `ILIKE` in `catalog/schema.py`).

Redeploy the panel image for this to take effect. The `ALTER` is `IF NOT EXISTS` and the `UPDATE` only fills nulls, so the retry is safe.

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# EC2 images. Default target `panel`: no Playwright, no Tectonic.
# `tectonic` does not follow app-code layers. Deploy reuses the previous
# mcp image for this stage when the binary version matches.
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm AS tectonic

ARG TECTONIC_VERSION=0.16.9

# Warm the TeX bundle so the first production PDF render does not download it.
COPY deploy/ec2/tectonic-warm.tex /tmp/tectonic-warm/warm.tex
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    && ARCH="$(dpkg --print-architecture)" \
    && case "$ARCH" in \
         amd64) TECTONIC_TARGET=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu ;; \
         arm64) REDACTED ;; \
         *) echo "unsupported arch: $ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
       esac \
    && curl -fsSL "https://github.com/tectonic-typesetting/tectonic/releases/download/tectonic%40${TECTONIC_VERSION}/tectonic-${TECTONIC_VERSION}-${TECTONIC_TARGET}.tar.gz" \
         | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin tectonic \
    && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/tectonic \
    && tectonic --outdir /tmp/tectonic-warm /tmp/tectonic-warm/warm.tex \
    && rm -rf /tmp/tectonic-warm \
    && apt-get purge -y curl \
    && apt-get autoremove -y \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

content.text:
The apt and Tectonic download runs on every code deploy because that step was built on top of the app image. Any change under `relocation_jobs/` invalidated it, so BuildKit rebuilt the layer and fetched Debian packages and Tectonic again.

Tectonic is now its own image stage. The deploy reuses the Tectonic binary and TeX cache already in `relocation-mcp:ec2` when that image has the same version (`0.16.9`) and `/root/.cache/Tectonic`. The bake log should show `reusing tectonic 0.16.9 from relocation-mcp:ec2`, and the `apt-get` step should not run.

A version change, or a missing cache directory, still builds that stage and downloads once. Redeploy for this to take effect.
